runs.title: COP31 ends with no deal: the official word
runs.prompt: The COP31 climate summit has reportedly ended without any deal after talks broke down. Find out what the summit was meant to agree, why the talks collapsed, and what the official organisers or the UN have said. Start with the UN's official climate site and major news outlets.
runs.answer: COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye (co-presided by Türkiye's Murat Kurum and Australia's Chris Bowen) was meant to deliver a consensus political package covering the launch of the second five-yearly Global Stocktake (concluding 2028), language on accelerating the transition away from fossil fuels agreed at COP28, climate finance ("who pays"), adaptation, a "just transition", the 1.5°C goal, electrification (Türkiye's "35x35" goal of 35% electricity in final energy use by 2035, backed by 75 countries) and science/IPCC timing — 21 issues were still unresolved in the final week. It collapsed on Sunday 22 November 2026 after two weeks plus two days of overtime — the longest-running UN climate summit on record — because agreement could not be reached on fossil fuels: explicit references to moving away from fossil fuels were stripped from successive draft texts, and a bloc of European, African, Latin American and Pacific countries formally objected to the final text as a weakening of previous commitments. UN Secretary-General António Guterres called it a "deeply disappointing" setback but insisted "there may be no consensus in the negotiating room, there is no ambiguity in the science," warning t

runs.prompt: Two tankers are reported ablaze near the Strait of Hormuz after hitting mines, and this is a developing story. runs.answer: Pick Al Jazeera (aljazeera.com). It is the only candidate that actually carried this developing story: the tanker mine attack was its lead item, updated minutes earlier, backed by a filed report, "Tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz as Iran tightens grip on shipping," which gives the UKMTO account (two vessels hit by projectiles minutes apart off Oman, one ablaze), damage details, "no casualties reported," and the Iranian navy's claim that a tanker with its transponder off entered a restricted area and hit a naval mine, plus a Tehran correspondent's analysis. Reuters and AP were unreadable to me (Reuters returned a 401 JS/anti-adblock wall, AP a 403 Cloudflare challenge), and BBC News had no coverage at all — its search returned nothing on Hormuz tankers newer than 15 September. Caveat: Al Jazeera does not name the two vessels and no casualties are reported, and its live blog body did not render as readable text, so the "two more tankers" detail is headline-level only.
